title: oven-roasted greek beef pastitsio
description: A classic Greek dish featuring a crispy, cheesy, and flavorful bechamel sauce, all on a bed of tender beef and pasta, without sacrificing any of the traditional Greek flavors. A vegan version is easily achieved by substituting the lamb with portobello mushrooms.
instructions: Cook the pasta according to the package instructions and set it aside.
In a large pan, heat the olive oil over medium heat and sauté the onion and garlic until softened.
Add the ground beef to the pan and cook until browned, breaking it up into small pieces as it cooks.
Stir in the kombu-cold-extract and cook for an additional 2 minutes.
In a separate saucepan, make the bechamel sauce by melting the butter over medium heat and whisking in the flour.
Gradually whisk in the beef broth and bring the mixture to a simmer.
Reduce the heat to low and cook for 5 minutes, or until the sauce thickens.
In a large bowl, combine the cooked pasta, beef mixture, and bechamel sauce. Mix well to combine.
Transfer the pasta mixture to a 9x13 inch baking dish.
Top the pasta with the crumbled feta cheese and grated parmesan cheese.
Dot the top of the cheese with the goose fat.
Bake the pastitsio in the preheated oven for 25-30 minutes, or until the cheese is golden brown and bubbly.
Remove the pastitsio from the oven and let it cool for 10-15 minutes before serving.
